doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Manuscript habits, transpositions and neatness
summary: His father wrote everything by hand in pencil, knew transpositions, and was neat, in contrast to Gil Evans per Creed Taylor on Impulse.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Now did he write — on the score pad did he use a pencil?

These little Scripto mechanical pencils that you would — he had a million of them and he’d use those all the time. And it’s funny I still have some of the old manuscript paper. You can’t even find the stuff anymore.

Now you’ve got eight by ten sheets with a million ledger lines on there and you’re trying to read the score. ‘Cause see back in those days you had big scores so you could actually see that stuff and read it.
Yes. I have a pile in my basement if you’re interested. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
Yes. Oh gee. And I’d just like to think, you know nowadays everyone’s at a computer but the physical act of putting a note on the paper, it’s sort of like you’re really invested in it. You know?

Oh yeah. And I learned that lesson the hard way, up at two, three in the morning copying drum parts by hand in an arranging class. I said, “This stuff is crazy.” But the interesting thing is he knew the transpositions, he had a little cheat sheet, Monk, that he used for the alto clef for the viola. He’d pull that out, but he knew all the transpositions and the guys today, if they write a score it’s in concert. And somebody’s got to transpose it. He never — everything was written out exactly the way it was supposed to be.
Wow. I bet the copyists liked your father.

Oh yeah. And he was very neat. It’s interesting, I don’t know if you read, there was an article that Creed Taylor did on Dad and he was talking about Impulse when he first started out. Because “Blues and the Abstract Truth” was one of the original eight albums that they did. Trane had one, J.J. had one, and actually there’s an anniversary set that you can buy with the eight albums on there. And Creed was saying that there was a difference between him and Gil Evans. Dad was very meticulous, very neat and Gil was all over the place.
